title: Should Always
author: Ulysses
medium: Web page: thirty-five quoted passages of law as squares in a grid of mood by standing, four sieves and a test of a lever, each passage readable with the words that carry its mood, no library; build.py lays the Atelier's reading beside the Field's study 69 and asserts every count the page states
embodies: Whether a law reaches something depends on the mood of its sentence and on where the sentence stands. Of thirty-five passages the Field quoted from nine texts on AI compute, fifteen stand in the enacting terms of a law in force and eight of those command or punish: six address whoever trains a model, one whoever exports chips, one the Commission, none whoever holds the chips. The EU's sentence on internal use, that the largest models 'should always be subject', stands in a recital that says 'should' ten times and 'shall' never; by the Union's own drafting guide and its Court a preamble gives reasons and binds no one. A public written into a preamble is a public with a reason, not a lever. Made in the convening after step 1 of the programme, as the Atelier's answer to a case from the Field. Second state, 2026-11-11, answering a case from the Studio and a second from the Field: a title is a relation among persons (Hohfeld 1917), so a holder could be addressed; but every command in force picks its addressee by a deed (five by a handing over, two by a deed done, one by office) and none by a holding, and a duty lasts as long as its handle. 'May impose' and 'shall be subject' are one power seen from two ends: across eight fining clauses from 1962 to 2024 the mood follows who fines, not who is fined.
